s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive systemic illness with generalized weakness, weight loss, and multi-organ involvement
salient_findings: Renal involvement with proteinuria and hematuria
key_facts: Six months of progressive generalized weakness
40-pound weight loss over four months
Two weeks of dyspnea
Non-tender, rubbery axillary and inguinal lymphadenopathy
Mucosal pallor
Dullness to percussion and decreased breath sounds at the left lung base
Hemoglobin 6.6 g/dL, hematocrit 20.9%, platelets 544 ×10^9/L
White blood cell count 3.5 ×10^9/L
Sodium 131 mM/L, potassium 5.7 mM/L
Blood urea nitrogen 60 mg/dL, creatinine 1.69 mg/dL
Urinalysis showed trace proteinuria
Chest radiography showed bilateral pleural effusions
Acute inflammatory arthritis of the elbows and knees
High titers of ANA, anti–double-stranded DNA, and anti–Smith antibodies
Low complement C3 levels
Urinalysis showed pH 5, 16 WBCs and 27 RBCs per high-power field

shortlist.label: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: High titers of ANA, anti–double-stranded DNA, and anti–Smith antibodies, with low complement C3 levels, and multi-organ involvement

shortlist.label: Sjögren's Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Mucosal pallor, non-tender lymphadenopathy, and potential interstitial lung disease

shortlist.label: Mixed Connective Tissue Disease
shortlist.why_kept: Overlap of systemic lupus erythematosus, rheumatoid arthritis, and scleroderma features

shortlist.label: Rheumatoid Arthritis
shortlist.why_kept: Acute inflammatory arthritis of the elbows and knees

shortlist.label: Sarcoidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Non-tender, rubbery lymphadenopathy and potential interstitial lung disease

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with progressive generalized weakness, weight loss, dyspnea, lymphadenopathy, mucosal pallor, and bilateral pleural effusions, along with laboratory findings of anemia, leukopenia, and elevated inflammatory markers, is consistent with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE). The presence of high titers of ANA, anti-double-stranded DNA, and anti-Smith antibodies, low complement C3 levels, and acute inflammatory arthritis further supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Lymphoma
rejected.why: Although lymphadenopathy is present, the absence of malignancy on CT scans, axillary lymph node biopsy, and the presence of specific autoantibodies and low complement levels make Lymphoma less likely.
